prompt: According to IAS 38 regarding the accounting for research and development costs it is CORRECT to say that …

options.text: Research and development costs have to be recognised as intangible assets if certain criteria of IAS 38 are met
Research costs have to be expensed; development costs have to be recognised as an intangible asset if the criteria of IAS 38 are met
Research and development costs have to be expensed regardless of the criteria of IAS 38
Research costs have to be recognised as intangible assets if certain criteria are met and development costs have to be expensed

explanation: Research never meets the recognition criteria (future benefits cannot be demonstrated) → expense. Development costs MUST be capitalised once all IAS 38 criteria are met (exam 2019 and 2024).

prompt: In which statement of Lumen Games can you find the staff costs expensed? Indicate the amount.
modelAnswer: Not on the face of the income statement: Lumen presents expenses by FUNCTION (cost of sales, R&D, selling, G&A), so staff costs are spread across these lines. They are disclosed in the notes (Note 7): 1,050 M€ (wages 820 + social charges 230). Under the function method IAS 1 requires such nature information in the notes.
keyPoints: Income statement is by function → staff costs not visible as a line

basis.ref: im Stil von Altklausur 2024, Part 5 (fiktiver Abschluss statt Ubisoft)

steps.title: Check how the income statement is presented
steps.why: Lumen shows cost of sales, R&D, selling and G&A expenses → presentation BY FUNCTION. Staff costs are therefore spread over these lines and not visible on the face of the income statement.

steps.title: Look in the notes
steps.why: IAS 1 requires entities that present by function to disclose additional information on the nature of expenses, including employee benefits expense, in the notes.
lines: Note 7: wages and salaries 820 + social charges 230 = 1,050
steps.result: Staff costs 1,050 M€, disclosed in the notes (Note 7)

topic: Cash capital increase from the statements
prompt: Was there a cash capital increase in N? If yes, specify its terms (increase in share capital, share premium, cash received, number of shares).
modelAnswer: Yes. Share capital rose from 13.0 to 15.4 (+2.4 M€) and share premium from 1,090.0 to 1,207.6 (+117.6 M€); the cash flow statement shows 'Proceeds from capital increase' of 120 M€ = 2.4 + 117.6. With a par value of €0.10, 24 million new shares were issued at an average price of €5.00 (120 / 24).

basis.ref: im Stil von Altklausur 2024, Part 5 (fiktiver Abschluss statt Ubisoft)

steps.title: Compare the equity lines
lines: Share capital: 15.4 − 13.0 = +2.4
Total increase in equity from shares: 120.0

steps.title: Confirm with the cash flow statement
steps.why: A CASH capital increase must appear in financing activities. 'Proceeds from capital increase' = 120 = 2.4 + 117.6 → the increase was paid in cash (not, e.g., a share dividend or a share-based acquisition).
steps.result: Yes – cash capital increase of 120 M€

steps.title: Derive the terms
lines: Number of new shares = increase in share capital / par value = 2.4 M€ / €0.10 = 24 million
Issue price per share = 120 M€ / 24 million = €5.00 (par €0.10 + premium €4.90)
steps.result: 24 m shares at €5.00: capital +2.4, premium +117.6, cash +120

topic: D&A and provisions in the cash flow statement
prompt: Explain why 'depreciation, amortisation, provisions' appears as a positive amount in the statement of cash flows.
modelAnswer: Lumen uses the indirect method: operating cash flow starts from net income and adds back expenses that did not cause a cash outflow. Depreciation, amortisation (e.g. of capitalised game development costs) and additions to provisions reduced net income by 900 M€ but no cash left the company in N, so they are added back (positive amount).
keyPoints: Indirect method starts from net income
They are added back to reconcile to operating cash flow

basis.ref: im Stil von Altklausur 2024, Part 5 (fiktiver Abschluss statt Ubisoft)

steps.title: Identify the method
steps.why: The operating cash flow starts with net income → INDIRECT method: net income is reconciled to cash by removing non-cash items and working-capital changes.

steps.title: Explain the add-back
steps.why: Depreciation, amortisation (e.g. of capitalised game development) and additions to provisions reduced net income by 900, but no cash left the company for them in N (the cash went out when the assets were bought). To get back to cash, they are added back.
steps.result: Non-cash expense → added back (positive) in the indirect method

prompt: Does Lumen have significant influence over any associates? List all items in the financial statements that support your answer.
modelAnswer: Yes. Balance sheet: 'Investments in associates' 35 (31 in N−1) – the equity method is used for entities under significant influence. Income statement: 'Share of profit of associates' 4. Cash flow statement: 'Share of profit of associates, net of dividends' (−4) is deducted because it is a non-cash income.
keyPoints: Adjustment in the cash flow statement

basis.ref: im Stil von Altklausur 2024, Part 5 (fiktiver Abschluss statt Ubisoft)

steps.title: Recall the rule
steps.why: Significant influence (typically 20–50% of voting rights) → associate → equity method (IAS 28). So look for the equity-method footprints in all statements.

steps.title: Collect the evidence
lines: Balance sheet: 'Investments in associates' 35 (N−1: 31)
Income statement: 'Share of profit of associates' +4
Cash flow statement: 'Share of profit of associates, net of dividends' −4 (non-cash income removed)
steps.result: Yes – Lumen has associates under significant influence

prompt: Are all Lumen subsidiaries 100% owned? Justify your answer.
modelAnswer: No. The balance sheet shows non-controlling interests of 12 (11 in N−1) in equity, and the income statement attributes 1 of net income to non-controlling interests. NCI only exist if minority shareholders hold part of at least one fully consolidated subsidiary.

basis.ref: im Stil von Altklausur 2024, Part 5 (fiktiver Abschluss statt Ubisoft)

steps.title: Look for non-controlling interests
steps.why: NCI only arise when a fully consolidated subsidiary is not 100% owned: the minority shareholders' share of its equity and result is shown separately.
lines: Balance sheet: non-controlling interests 12 (N−1: 11) within equity
Income statement: net income attributable to NCI +1
steps.result: No – at least one subsidiary is not wholly owned

prompt: Does Lumen use leasing to finance any of its assets? List all items that support your answer.
modelAnswer: Yes. Balance sheet: right-of-use assets 180 and lease liabilities 195 (IFRS 16). Income statement: interest on lease liabilities (9) within financial expense (depreciation of ROU assets within the functional lines). Cash flow statement: 'Repayment of lease liabilities' (40) in financing activities.
keyPoints: Interest on lease liabilities / repayment of lease liabilities

basis.ref: im Stil von Altklausur 2024, Part 5 (fiktiver Abschluss statt Ubisoft)

steps.title: Recall IFRS 16
steps.why: Lessees recognise a right-of-use asset and a lease liability; the expense is split into depreciation and interest; repayments are financing cash flows.

steps.title: Collect the evidence
lines: Balance sheet: right-of-use assets 180; lease liabilities 195
Income statement: interest on lease liabilities 9 (in net financial expense); ROU depreciation inside the functional lines
Cash flow statement: repayment of lease liabilities −40 (financing)
steps.result: Yes – Lumen leases assets (IFRS 16 items in all three statements)

modelAnswer: Yes, most likely small ones. The amounts are small compared with the group's size.

Goodwill not amortised → increase from acquisitions

lines: 'Acquisition of subsidiaries, net of cash acquired' −18

steps.title: Look at goodwill
steps.why: Goodwill is not amortised; it only increases through new business combinations (or currency translation) and decreases through impairment or disposals.
lines: Goodwill 230 → 241 (+11)

prompt: In which statement of Ubisoft can you find the staff costs expensed? Indicate the amount if possible.
modelAnswer: Not on the face of the income statement: Ubisoft presents expenses by FUNCTION (cost of sales, R&D costs, marketing costs, administrative and IT costs), so staff costs are spread over these lines. Under the function method IAS 1 requires the nature of expenses, including employee benefits expense, to be disclosed in the NOTES – the amount can only be read there (the notes are not reproduced in the exam). The only staff-related figure visible in the statements is the cost of stock-based compensation (59.6 M€) added back in the cash flow statement and shown in the statement of changes in equity (IFRS 2: 59.6).
keyPoints: Income statement by function → no staff cost line
Staff costs are disclosed in the notes (nature of expenses)
Only share-based compensation 59.6 visible (cash flow statement, changes in equity)

steps.title: How is the income statement presented?
steps.why: Lines are cost of sales, R&D, marketing, administrative and IT costs → presentation BY FUNCTION. Staff costs are included in each of these functions.

steps.title: Where to look instead
steps.why: IAS 1: an entity classifying by function must disclose additional information on the nature of expenses (depreciation, employee benefits) in the notes.
lines: Notes → employee benefits expense
Visible in the statements: stock-based compensation 59.6 (cash flow statement, changes in equity)
steps.result: Staff costs: in the notes; amount not shown on the face of the statements

pitfalls: Looking for a 'personnel costs' line – it only exists in an income statement BY NATURE.

topic: Cash capital increase from the statements
prompt: Was there a cash capital increase in the year ended 31 March 2024? If yes, specify its terms by indicating the items concerned (increase in share capital, share premium and cash received).
modelAnswer: Yes. In the statement of changes in equity the line 'Change in the share capital of the parent company' shows capital +0.1 and premiums +44.8 = 44.9 M€ (balance sheet: capital 9.7 → 9.9, premiums 630.2 → 675.0). The cash flow statement shows in financing activities 'Funds received from shareholders in capital increases' of 44.9 M€ → the shares were paid in cash. Terms: share capital +0.1 M€ (par value of the new shares), share premium +44.8 M€, cash +44.9 M€.
keyPoints: Same 44.9 in the statement of changes in equity

steps.title: Equity lines
lines: Capital: 9.9 − 9.7 = +0.1 (rounded)
Changes in equity: 'Change in the share capital of the parent company' 0.1 + 44.8 = 44.9

steps.title: Was it paid in cash?
steps.why: A cash capital increase must appear in financing cash flows; a share dividend or shares issued for an acquisition would not.
lines: Cash flow statement: 'Funds received from shareholders in capital increases' 44.9
steps.result: Yes – cash capital increase of 44.9 M€: capital +0.1, premium +44.8

pitfalls: Taking the increase in total equity (+396.7) – it also contains net income, share-based payments, own shares etc.
Treating the sale of own shares (11.5) as a capital increase – treasury shares are not new shares.

topic: Indirect method – non-cash expenses added back
prompt: Explain why the line 'Net amortisation and depreciation on property, plant and equipment and intangible assets' appears as a positive amount (776.0) in Ubisoft's statement of cash flows.
modelAnswer: Ubisoft uses the INDIRECT method: operating cash flow starts from consolidated net income (157.9). Depreciation and amortisation were deducted as expenses to compute net income but cause no cash outflow (the cash left when the assets were bought – shown in investing activities). They are therefore added back as a positive amount. The same logic applies to provisions: an increase is a non-cash expense (added back), a release is non-cash income (deducted – here −4.6).
keyPoints: Indirect method starts from net income
D&A is an expense without cash outflow → added back
Cash outflow was in investing activities when the asset was bought
Provisions: increase added back, release deducted (−4.6)

steps.title: Starting point
steps.why: Indirect method: net income → adjust for non-cash items and working capital changes.
lines: Consolidated profit 157.9

steps.title: Why add D&A back?
steps.why: Depreciation/amortisation reduced net income but no cash left the company in the year; the cash outflow happened when the asset was acquired (investing activities, e.g. payments for developments 887.0).
lines: + 776.0 net amortisation and depreciation
steps.result: Positive amount = reversal of a non-cash expense

pitfalls: Saying that depreciation 'generates' cash – it only does not consume cash.

Associates (significant influence, IAS 28) are accounted for with the equity method, which would show up in three places – all of them are empty ('—') for both years: balance sheet 'Investments in associates' —; income statement 'Share of profit of associates' —; cash flow statement 'Share of profit of associates' —.
keyPoints: Equity method items would show associates
Income statement: share of profit of associates —
Cash flow statement: share of profit of associates —

steps.title: Where associates appear
steps.why: Significant influence → equity method: one line on the asset side and the share of profit in the income statement (reversed in the indirect cash flow statement).
lines: Balance sheet: 'Investments in associates' — / —
Income statement: 'Share of profit of associates' — / —
Cash flow statement: 'Share of profit of associates' — / —
steps.result: No associates with any value → no significant influence reported

prompt: Are all Ubisoft subsidiaries 100% owned? Justify your answer.
modelAnswer: No. Non-controlling interests exist, which is only possible if some subsidiaries are not wholly owned: balance sheet NCI 2.6 M€ (3.5); net income attributable to NCI 0.1 (−0.6); comprehensive income attributable to NCI 0.1; a separate NCI column in the statement of changes in equity, including 'Changes in ownership interests in subsidiaries without gain/loss of control' (NCI −0.9: Ubisoft bought out part of the minorities) and a 'Commitment to purchase minority shareholders' shares'. The amounts are very small, so the minority stakes are marginal.
keyPoints: NCI column in the statement of changes in equity
Changes in ownership without loss of control (−0.9) and commitment to buy minority shares

steps.title: Logic
steps.why: Full consolidation integrates 100% of a subsidiary; the share of equity and profit not owned by the parent is shown as non-controlling interest. NCI ≠ 0 ⇒ at least one subsidiary is not 100% owned.

steps.title: Evidence
lines: Balance sheet: non-controlling interests 2.6 (3.5)
Income statement: net income attributable to NCI 0.1 (−0.6)
Comprehensive income: attributable to NCI 0.1
Changes in equity: NCI column; ownership change −0.9; commitment to purchase minority shares
steps.result: Not all subsidiaries are 100% owned (but minorities are small)

prompt: Does Ubisoft use leasing to finance any of its assets? List all items in the financial statements that support your answer.
modelAnswer: Yes. Under IFRS 16 the lessee recognises a right-of-use asset and a lease liability: balance sheet 'Right-of-use assets' 278.4 M€ (271.9); the lease liabilities are included in 'Long-term / Short-term borrowings and other financial liabilities'; cash flow statement (financing) 'Refund of borrowings in relation to leases' (43.9) – the repayment of the lease liability. The depreciation of the right-of-use assets is part of the depreciation added back in operating cash flow, and the interest on lease liabilities is part of the interest expense.
keyPoints: Lease liabilities within borrowings / financial liabilities
Financing cash flow: refund of borrowings in relation to leases (43.9)
Depreciation of ROU and interest in the income statement

steps.title: IFRS 16 footprint of a lessee
lines: Asset: right-of-use assets 278.4 (271.9)
Liability: lease liabilities inside borrowings and other financial liabilities
Cash flow (financing): refund of borrowings in relation to leases (43.9)
Income statement: depreciation of ROU + interest on the lease liability

topic: New acquisitions – evidence in the statements
prompt: Do you think Ubisoft made any new (small) acquisitions in the year ended 31 March 2024? List all items in the financial statements that support your answer.
modelAnswer: Probably not. An acquisition of a subsidiary would show (1) a cash outflow 'Change in scope' in investing activities – it is '—' in 2024 (but (30.8) in 2023, when Ubisoft did acquire companies); (2) new goodwill – goodwill is practically unchanged (73.2 → 73.3, the +0.1 is likely an exchange difference); (3) a 'Change in scope' line in the statement of changes in equity – also '—'. So no new acquisitions in 2024.
keyPoints: Cash flow statement: change in scope — in 2024 (30.8 in 2023)
Changes in equity: change in scope —

steps.title: Where an acquisition leaves traces
lines: Investing cash flow: 'Change in scope' (price paid net of cash acquired)
Balance sheet: new goodwill / brands
Changes in equity: 'Change in scope' (e.g. new NCI)

steps.title: Read Ubisoft's figures
lines: Change in scope (cash flow): — (2023: −30.8)
Goodwill: 73.3 vs 73.2
Change in scope (equity): —
steps.result: No new acquisitions in 2024 (there were some in 2023)

pitfalls: Reading the large increase in other intangible assets (+299) as an acquisition – it comes from capitalised game developments (payments for developments 887.0).
